findings.evidence: template/scripts/managed_task.py: `payload = run(["git", "show", f"{commit}:{directory / PROVENANCE}"], root).stdout; (local / PROVENANCE).write_text(payload, encoding="utf-8")`. The JSON provenance is probably unaffected. The new writer-baseline entry in tests/test_shared_writer_guard.py exists only because of this copy, so parsing the blob directly would avoid both the copy and the entry.
findings.summary: resolve_committed_lineage decodes provenance via run(...).stdout as text and rewrites it with write_text, so it depends on the run() helper's text decoding and newline handling. It does not copy the exact git blob bytes.

findings.evidence: execute_requirement.py `_done_child_is_delivered` calls managed_task.target_main(integration) on every call. resolve_committed_lineage runs `git ls-tree -r --name-only <commit> -- openspec/changes`, which lists every archived file. design.md accepts this as 'a handful of children'. It could be a problem for large archives or long-running recovery loops.
findings.summary: _done_child_is_delivered runs `git fetch --prune` and a recursive `ls-tree -r` over openspec/changes for each child it checks. Cost grows with the archive size and the number of children.
